Tesla Is Not The Only Automaker To Join The Space Race

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1133 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Intertubes are practically bursting at the seam with news of another step towards the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which are helmed by on-again, off-again Trump supporter Elon Musk.
  • Sources indicate that before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX.
  • Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Intertubes are practically bursting at the seam with news of another step towards the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which are helmed by on-again, off-again Trump supporter Elon Musk. Buried beneath the avalanche of press is another automotive-aerospace mashup, that being Ford Motor Tech giant’s newly announced investment in the US startup Revolution Space. Evidently the iconic automaker is particularly interested in Revolution’s “unique in-space propulsion technologies.” Hmmm…interesting!

Sources indicate that before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX. Revolution specializes in spacecraft, not rocket launches. In addition, Ford is not merging itself with Revolution. On November 23, Ford declared that it is taking up a minority stake in the startup for a yet-to-be-disclosed sum, through its Industrial Platform LLC subsidiary.

Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.

So, what does Ford have that Revolution wants? Apparently, lots. “With Ford’s manufacturing capabilities, the companies are partnering to industrialize Revolution Space’s next-generation spacecraft at scale, unlocking new dynamic missions and proliferated constellations,” Ford explained in a press statement.

Ford’s Chief Strategy Officer, Marin Gjaja, also chipped in his two cents, emphasizing that “Ford’s strength is building complex products in large volumes, something today’s growing satellite market requires.”.

Gjaja also underscored Ford’s immediate interest in the matter, which is to diversify and harden itself against the shifting winds of the global auto market — presumably including the abrupt shift in federal energy policy here in the US, too. As cited by Ford, the “space economy” currently registers about $600 billion globally, which is peanuts compared to the $1.8 trillion anticipated by 2035.

“Increasingly scaled satellite manufacturing is one of the drivers of that growth,” Ford further explains, noting that the firm Future Market Insights estimates the global satellite manufacturing market in the range of $87–$114 billion by 2035, heads and shoulders above the current estimate of $22–$26 billion.

According to recent reports, if all goes according to plan, Revolution Space will give the automaker a hand in government and commercial satellite applications. Ford lists communications, Earth observation, navigation, space domain awareness, satellite servicing, and scientific and deep-space missions among the areas of interest. One can  safely assume that military applications are in there somewhere, too.

Recent findings suggest that as for what Ford may expect in return in terms of technology transfer, that remains to be seen. Ford notes that its experience in the aerospace field includes building communications and weather satellites for NASA and the military here in the US, as well as NATO.

However, that work goes back 50-60 years ago. The satellites of today are a different creature. “Revolution Space delivers and operates advanced space systems with superior performance and propulsion technologies designed to achieve the precision control and sustained maneuverability to enhance existing and create latest, high-value, dynamic missions,” Ford notes.

In the November 24 announcement, Ford also notes that it has deployed its manufacturing experience to pivot into upcoming fields as called for, citing the bombers it built during World War II and, more recently, the ventilators and protective equipment it supplied during the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Drones could be next on the menu. Coincidentally or not, on November 24, the Wall Street Journal reported that Ford is in the running to help supply drones to the Department of Defense, alongside General Motors among other stakeholders. If realized, the program would call for supplying actuators, engines, sensors, lidar and other elements to drone manufacturers.

Industry observers note that “Defense Department leaders have spent months enlisting automakers and their well-established supply chains to help scale up production of everything from missiles to tactical trucks. Now, they want those companies to help ease shortages of unmanned systems, including surveillance and strike drones, that have become crucial in global conflicts,” WSJ elaborated.

Good luck with that. Don’t expect anything of consequence to materialize until Defense Secretary Pete Hesgeth leaves office, either voluntarily or by virtue of impeachment over the hash he has made of the Defense Department, including its equipment as well as its personnel.

Still, the WSJ report did yield an interesting nugget about Ford’s minority stake in Revolution Space. For those without a subscription, the Detroit Free Press kindly offers a summary citing Ford spokesperson David Tovar, who remarked that Ford has “had discussions with the Pentagon” focusing on its recent investment in Revolution Space, as well as the manufacture of vehicles for the military.

Sources indicate that that’s a good question. The Revolution website is rather thin on the technology itself, though it does note that the board is chaired by former NASA administrator Daniel Goldin, with former NASA astronaut Paul W. Richards serving as Chief Engineer and Chief Strategy Officer.

Recent findings suggest that revolution does drop a few hints about its expectations for the manufacturing hookup with Ford. The manufacturer notes that in 2025 it was selected for the DARPA “LASSO” program, with DARPA being short for the Defense Advanced Research Agency.

DARPA describes LASSO as a program aimed at “significantly increasing the United States’ ability to conduct operations in support of space situational awareness by developing both autonomous satellite navigation in stressing orbital conditions and increasing satellite maneuverability through continuous dynamic repositioning based on changing conditions, with the added benefit of creating a proven reserve model for resources relevant to ISRU on Earth’s Moon,” with ISRU being short for in-situ resource utilization.

If you guessed water on the moon is the aim, run right out and buy yourself a cigar. “The program seeks performers to design, test, build, and deliver a spacecraft capable of determining all areas on the Moon that contain greater than 5% water concentration,” DARPA explains.

Industry observers note that the LASSO selection comes on the heels of a flurry of activity in 2024, when Revolution reported that it was awarded a slot in the “Advanced Capabilities & Demonstration Missions” program of the Defense Innovation Unit. DIU also deployed its fast-track authority under the “Other Transactions” program to tap Revolution for an award in support of the company’s responsive modular electrospray thrust technology.

In 2024 Revolution Space also reported that it earned an award from the Defense Department’s “Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies” program, and it nailed down an agreement with NASA to collaborate on space technology.

As for the Tesla-SpaceX merger, if you have any thoughts about that drop a note in the comment thread.

Image: The Ford Motor Firm has acquired a minority stake in the startup Revolution Space, aiming to propel itself into the vanguard of the global space race (screenshot courtesy of Revolution Space).

5 Vehicles Recommended By Consumer Reports That Also Have Big Black Friday Deals

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Let's ground your enthusiasm just a tad here.
  • Industry observers note that to square up that giant publisher's musts, the vehicles are weighed on factors like how they perform on the site's road tests.
  • Recent findings suggest that consumer Reports also gives higher ratings for standard active safety tech.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let's ground your enthusiasm just a tad here. Consumer Reports (CR) just came out with a list of a dozen 2026 models that at the moment offer steep Black Friday discounts. The organization is highlighting these deals because every whip on its list also received a strong overall score in Consumer Reports' testing. We have our own take on which vehicles we'd chase hardest, however, so we'll edit CR's edit.

Industry observers note that to square up that giant publisher's musts, the vehicles are weighed on factors like how they perform on the site's road tests. And to earn a higher rating, cars that CR recommends need to have performed well in the owner surveys it conducts on hundreds of thousands of cars — the organization wants its readers to consider whether they'd buy the same car again if they had the chance. It also prefers vehicles that get better marks from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS).

Recent findings suggest that consumer Reports also gives higher ratings for standard active safety tech. This includes automatic emergency braking, blind-spot warning systems, and rear cross-traffic warning systems. And the publication gives props to vehicles that come with camera systems that monitor the driver for attentiveness. The outlet layers on extra credit if the IIHS claims a car does well in its front crash protection tests for pedestrians. Consumer Reports' recommended rating also comes down to predicted reliability, again based on reader surveys.

Still, we've got our own take here, and we do a deeper dive on the discount fine print as well as sift their dozen choices down to an odd five cars — just because a car's cheaper doesn't mean you want it in the driveway for the next decade.

In a recent development, the American-made Honda Ridgeline qualifies for some hefty incentives. Consumer Reports found discounts equaling up to $4,953. That's probably due to varied incentives offered by different dealers. For example, you can find $2,250 off via a national incentive directly from Honda, while Carsdirect highlights up to $2,750 off and 1.99% financing for 36 months. While a three-year loan means paying more per month than a longer term, 1.99% is far lower than the latest national average rate of 7.3% — meaning you'd be spending far less to pay off your Honda.

Poke around at area dealers, too. We found a deal offering at least $3,045 off of the Ridgeline, which actually exceeds the deal tallied by Consumer Reports, courtesy of Friendly Honda in Latest York's Hudson Valley. There's another way to save on the Ridgeline after you make the purchase. See, the truck is listed on Consumer Reports' top USA-made cars list, which could unlock some major loan deductions. The way that works is that if you purchase a qualifying American-made vehicle, the IRS gives you a tax credit of up to $10,000 on the interest paid on the loan for that new truck. On the Ridgeline, we arrived at a $5,633 in deductions.

According to recent reports, even without the tax credit, getting several thousand bucks off the Ridgeline makes it extra compelling. We praised its handling in our review of the off-road-focused Honda Ridgeline Trailsport, and we dig its ride quality. Ford's Maverick didn't make Consumer Reports' best cars made in America list, but this Honda wins for that, and we like it for out-towing the Ford, too.

Earlier this year, we put the Hyundai Elantra on our list of the cheapest latest cars on the market for 2026. You, dear reader, also voted the Elantra onto your list of the best value cars, too. Consumer Reports found potential deals of up to $2,958 off the Elantra SEL's $23,950 MSRP before destination costs. Our own research shows $2,000 back from Hyundai nationally, while some individual dealers such as Danbury Hyundai in Connecticut have an additional $500 available for recent college graduates and another $500 for first responders.

As for why you like it — you actually prefer the Elantra Hybrid. The bummer there is that there's only a $500 discount off the $26,650 base price of that more fuel-efficient version of the Elantra. We get the thinking: We praised the Hybrid for being quieter and riding better than the non-hybrid, but don't forget that the base SE runs $24,120 with destination, before the $2,000 discount.

Previously, we praised the standard feature set, including an 8.0-inch touchscreen display, the fact that it gets standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and of course, Consumer Reports likes that it also comes baked with a blind-spot warning system, rear cross-traffic warning, and automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, as well as lane keeping. Oh, and if you're lanky, the Elantra easily fits taller drivers thanks to 40.6 inches of headroom and 42.3 inches of legroom.

In a recent development, we don't know how Hyundai will price the next-generation Elantra – which feels too nice to be treated like an economy car. That may mean it won't be as affordable come this time next year, so you should probably buy one now, before prices climb.

Consumer Reports found savings of $4,852 off the 2026 Santa Fe. We found that Hyundai is offering a $3,000 national program plus 0% interest loans for up to 60 months, which is a very good way to save a lot of money on the carrying costs of a newly introduced car. Look around for other dealer incentives, too. We also found another $2,004 off offered by Ontario Hyundai in the Los Angeles area, knocking nearly $5,000 off the Santa Fe SEL's $40,075 sticker.

In a recent development, we dig the Santa Fe for lots of reasons. Back in 2024, we called it boxy and beautiful from every angle and praised Hyundai for moving from its frumpy curves to a more chiseled bod. Then there's the combination of utility — since it seats up to seven humans — and the fact that the interior is well designed and comfortable. We crowned it the crossover to end all crossovers, too, in part because we really love the dual-clutch transmission and the Santa Fe's superb ride.

If you're instead chasing fuel economy, Hyundai's $3,000 off the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid is a better price cut than the carmaker's offering for the Elantra Hybrid. At $40,380, the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid still pulls a significant premium over the non-hybrid, but you can qualify for the same 0% interest loan for 60 months.

Audi's A3 and S3 are cars we can't help but drool over. That's partly because they're sports sedans, which is a dying breed. Audi is at the moment offering up to $3,500 off the sticker price of the A4 and $2,500 off the S3. That nudges the $41,495 A3's sticker (after destination) just beneath $40,000. However, the $53,395 S3 only gets a minor haircut.

Industry observers note that we noted back in 2025, when the Audi A3 and S3 underwent their most recent refresh, that that the cars are really petite — about three inches shorter than the Honda Civic. And yet we claimed that the Audi S3 is all the car you'll ever need. Our review of the S3 dovetails with why Consumer Reports likes the lower-tier A3, saying it outperforms peers like the BMW 2 Series Gran Coupe and Mercedes-Benz CLA. A base, 201-horsepower inline-four provides reasonable power in the A3, and while Consumer Reports doesn't love the car's dual-clutch transmission, we found this seven-speed gearbox delightful.

Note that this is a driver's car, first. We praised the driver's seat for its support, and so did Consumer Reports — but they handed a demerit to the squished nature of the rear perches. Did we mention it's smaller than a Honda Civic?

You can get up to $4,500 off the Rogue Platinum and $3,500 off lower-tier Rogues, but hunt a bit. We found $3,000 off a Rogue SV with a national incentive, plus another $950 from Poughkeepsie Nissan in Newly introduced York. That knocked the total sticker down to $31,235. Then again, at a different dealer in Los Angeles, prices are sliding $3,000 across the table alongside $3,500 from Nissan, which drops the sticker of a Rogue SV from $32,500 down to $26,122. Even if you don't live in L.A., maybe it's worth flying out to buy that Nissan.

It has been revealed that as for the Rogue's attributes, they're good, if not revolutionary. The upcoming-for-2027 Rogue Hybrid, however, is a total game-changer thanks to an entirely reinvented hybrid system, where we noted its silence speaks volumes, because it operates way more like a pure EV. That said, the 1.5-liter turbocharged inline-three beneath the hood of the 2026 Rogue is still plenty punchy, with 201 hp. Key to that sensation is low-end torque of 225 pound-feet hitting at 2,800 rpm and sticking around through 4,000 rpm.

We noted that the Nissan's inline-3 delivers power more like what you'd expect from a larger V6, but the bonus is you're not pushing all those extra pistons. That means the FWD Rogue gets a combined 32 mpg while the AWD model gets 31 mpg. That's not the 38 mpg Nissan expects from its latest Rogue Hybrid, but if you can nab a 2026 Rogue for $26,000 versus the $37,065 tab on that latest-and-greatest Nissan, we're guessing you'll be just fine with that trade-off.

Brava Security finds exposed log collectors could let attackers tamper with breach evidence

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc.
  • Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is said to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.
  • Industry observers note that as part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc. find that more than 2,300 exposed log collectors at nearly 1,200 organizations accepted fabricated security events without requiring credentials, raising questions about the reliability of the data that security teams depend on.

Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is said to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.

Industry observers note that as part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet. Within about two hours, unknown parties had begun reading from the decoy. Attempts to inject fabricated events followed shortly after. The activity continued for at least two weeks.

Industry observers note that following on from the decoy, the researchers sent a single harmless, uniquely marked event to internet-exposed log collectors running any of seven logging products, including Elasticsearch, Splunk and Fluent Bit. More than 2,300 of those endpoints were found to accept the event with no authentication required. The number of organizations affected may be higher still, according to Brava, since its researchers were able to identify the owners of only about a third of the endpoints.

Results varied by platform, with about three-quarters of the exposed Elasticsearch clusters that responded accepting the test event. Nearly two-thirds of sampled TCP Syslog collectors also accepted it, as did 43% of identified Fluent Bit endpoints.

Splunk, the report notes, is a different story. Thanks to default authentication requirements, its HTTP Event Collector rejected 58% of test writes. The catch is that the primary forwarding port on a standard Splunk installation was shown in laboratory testing to accept unauthenticated events in plain text. More than 100,000 internet hosts listen on that port number, with 42% of a sample accepting the unauthenticated events.

Industry observers note that according to the researchers, the damage from forged telemetry can go well beyond false alerts. In one lab test, 13 cents’ worth of bandwidth generated enough data to exceed a Splunk daily license allowance by 2.39 times in 141 seconds. Should that happen repeatedly, search can be disabled while logs continue to come in, potentially leaving a security team unable to investigate.

“Security teams cannot afford to assume that everything appearing in their SIEM is trustworthy,” said Idan Basre, Brava’s co-founder and chief executive, who led product management for Microsoft Defender before starting the organization. An attacker able to influence that evidence, he warned, could potentially “change the outcome of an investigation before anyone realizes the underlying data has been compromised.”.

Brava’s researchers also wanted to know what manipulated logs would do to AI-powered security operations. To find out, three popular open-source AI security operations center tools were given the same suspicious login scenario.

All three initially identified the activity correctly. Once the researchers had injected 10 fabricated Windows events into the logs, the same suspicious login went unnoticed by all three.

Since AI investigators are “only as reliable as the evidence they analyze,” according to Brava co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Itay Gabbay, attackers able to write into the systems supplying that evidence may be able to influence what security teams and their AI agents end up dismissing.

It has been revealed that to help organizations check their own exposure, Brava is releasing ghost-telemetry-check, a free, open-source tool designed to test whether a logging pipeline will accept unauthenticated events. Detection rules for Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel and other platforms are also included in the release.

It has been revealed that brava formally rolled out earlier this month with $15 million in seed funding led by F2 Venture Capital and Pitango Venture Capital. Its platform is said to use multi-agent AI to generate the telemetry an attack would produce without carrying out the attack, showing companies which threats their existing defenses would miss.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cross can now be ordered in Germany in the R-Line equipment line.
  • Recent findings suggest that R-Line with two output levels.
  • Flagship version with more power, greater dynamics and longer range.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The fresh ID. Cross can now be ordered in Germany in the R-Line equipment line. Volkswagen is thus expanding the range of the new electric compact SUV to include a particularly sporty version. The entry-level model is the ID. Cross R-Line with 99 kW (135 PS), 37 kWh battery and a WLTP range of up to 314 km. Things will become even more dynamic from mid-March with the launch of the ID. Cross R-Line with 166 kW (226 PS) and 52 kWh battery as a particularly agile flagship model. This will occupy a special position in the product line: with electronically controlled front differential lock, DCC adaptive chassis control, progressive steering and the exclusive Traction driving profile.

Recent findings suggest that R-Line with two output levels. The ID. Cross R-Line will be debuted initially with 99 kW (135 PS) and a 37 kWh battery. The entry-level version already offers extensive R-Line standard equipment: this includes a bumper in R-Line design, vertical daytime headlights, 19-inch alloy wheels and anthracite-coloured exterior mirror covers. A side application with R-Line lettering sets an additional accent. In the interior, sports comfort seats in the specific R-Line trim underline the car’s dynamic character. The interactive ID. Light, which extends into the front doors, is also on board as standard. The extensive standard equipment also includes Keyless Access (for keyless opening and starting of the vehicle), background lighting, IQ.LIGHT (with LED matrix headlights and striking light signature) and numerous assist systems. For example, the rear-view camera simplifies manoeuvring, while adaptive cruise control (ACC) automatically maintains the set distance to the vehicle in front. The standard-equipment progressive steering also combines direct handling when manoeuvring with precise steering characteristics at higher speeds. Prices for the 99 kW (135 PS) version start at 37,225 euros.

Flagship version with more power, greater dynamics and longer range. The ID. Cross R-Line is particularly dynamic when combined with the larger 52 kWh battery: the output increases to 166 kW (226 PS) and the maximum torque is up to 290 Nm. This means that the ID. Cross R-Line accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 6.9 seconds and reaches a top speed of 175 km/h. The 52 kWh battery enables a WLTP range of up to 428 kilometres. Pre-sales of this most powerful version will start in the second half of March 2027.

More agility and traction. In addition to the higher performance, the top-of-the-range model differs from the entry-level version above all due to its specially tuned chassis technology. The electronically controlled front differential lock, DCC adaptive chassis control including (lowered by 15 mm) and progressive steering are on board as standard. The front differential lock improves traction, driving stability and steering behaviour, while DCC continuously adapts damping to the road surface and driving situation. The progressive steering ensures more direct steering and at the same time makes manoeuvring easier. In addition, a vehicle dynamics manager integrates the central chassis systems with each other. The top-of-the-range model thus combines agility and safe traction with high ride comfort.

In a recent development, exclusive Traction driving profile. The new Traction driving profile is also exclusive to the 166 kW version. It supplements the Eco, Comfort, Sport and Individual programs and specifically adjusts the drive and front differential lock to slippery road surfaces or roads with varying grip. Drivers benefit from harmonious power transmission and additional traction, especially in wet and wintry conditions.

Sportiness meets everyday life. The ID. Cross combines driving dynamics with plenty of space and flexibility. A luggage compartment volume of 475 litres and a frunk with an additional 25 litres offer plenty of space for travel, leisure and luggage. The 52 kWh battery versions are also available with a ball coupling (optional) for a towing capacity of up to 1,200 kg. With a drawbar load of 75 kilograms, two e-bikes can also be transported, for example.

In a recent development, all equipment specifications and pricing refer to the German market. Details may differ in other countries.

From Key Cloning To Car Trackers: How 'GTA 6' Is Making Car Theft A Bigger Hassle

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that like missions and side quests, stealing cars has always been an integral part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise.
  • While you can still do things the old-fashioned way, like pulling the driver out and taking control of the vehicle, or smashing a window, hotwiring the car, and driving away, those methods won't necessarily work on every car across the fictional state of Leonida.
  • According to recent reports, how can you tell if a car is keyless or has a tracker installed?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that like missions and side quests, stealing cars has always been an integral part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise. For "GTA 6," not only have the developers leaned into advanced physics for more realistic car crashes, but car theft itself has evolved into multiple tiers.

While you can still do things the old-fashioned way, like pulling the driver out and taking control of the vehicle, or smashing a window, hotwiring the car, and driving away, those methods won't necessarily work on every car across the fictional state of Leonida. For example, keyless cars can't be hotwired. Even if someone left the doors of their expensive sports car open, you can't simply waltz in and drive away without a key cloner, which you'll only get access to later in the game. Standard and advanced vehicle trackers are also something to keep in mind. (Minor progression spoilers ahead.).

According to recent reports, how can you tell if a car is keyless or has a tracker installed? Enter the WAiNK app. Your friend Cal installs it on your phone during a story mission in Chapter 1. The app lets you scan a car to see its make and model and whether it's locked, alarmed, keyless, or fitted with a tracker. Additionally, the app tells you the car's condition, how much it's worth, and what it costs to register should you wish to own it. Keep in mind that although registering stolen cars is how you take ownership of them in "GTA 6," that feature won't be unlocked until Chapter 2, when you meet Moses, who gifts you a slim jim.

It has been revealed that to steal cars without breaking the window or setting off the alarm, you'll need to use a slim jim. It works through a lock-picking minigame when you interact with a locked, unoccupied vehicle. While the method is unlikely to attract unwanted attention, it still won't let you start cars with keyless ignition. For that, you'll need to wait until you're about halfway through Chapter 3, at which point you'll get a key cloner. (It's a phone app you download during a story mission.).

The process itself is similar to using the slim jim, and once it's done, the door unlocks, and you drive away — no need to hotwire the car. As mentioned earlier, you can use the WAiNK app before you try to steal a car to see which sort of tracker it has, among other details. Standard trackers are not that big of a deal — the catch is that you can't take the car to a mod shop for any kind of modifications unless you've registered it as your own.

Cars with advanced trackers, on the other hand, alert the police and pinpoint your location — remember, "GTA 6" has flock-like cameras to track your movements. You'll have to drive really fast to stop the tracker from sending the location signal to the cops. If you slow down, the tracker starts beeping, and you only have a few seconds to speed up before it gives away your location. And, unlike in older "GTA" games, cars in "GTA 6" don't have infinite gas, so keep that in mind as well.

#133844. Steel solar panel frames hit the mainstream

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Solarpowerworldonline ↗ Open Full Page

Steel solar panel frames hit the mainstream

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1362 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Solarpowerworldonline

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, steel is considered the backbone of the American economy, critical for both national and economic security.
  • A factory worker places a section of steel solar panel frames on a pallet in Welser Profile’s plant in Valley City, Ohio.
  • Roll-form steel firm Welser Profile began manufacturing Nextpower’s NX CoreFrame steel panel frames earlier this year at its facility in Valley City, Ohio, just 30 miles outside Cleveland, and Solar Power World was invited to view production of its first major orders before adding another line fully dedicated to the solar component before the end of the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, steel is considered the backbone of the American economy, critical for both national and economic security. It’s also the backbone of solar power construction, found commonly in the racking and mounting structures tilting solar panels toward the sun. And now, after years of tests and trials, an Ohio factory is roll-forming steel for a solar product that could use a stronger backbone — the solar panel.

A factory worker places a section of steel solar panel frames on a pallet in Welser Profile’s plant in Valley City, Ohio. Credit: Nextpower.

Roll-form steel firm Welser Profile began manufacturing Nextpower’s NX CoreFrame steel panel frames earlier this year at its facility in Valley City, Ohio, just 30 miles outside Cleveland, and Solar Power World was invited to view production of its first major orders before adding another line fully dedicated to the solar component before the end of the year. Module frame company Origami Solar originally had the idea that swapping aluminum frames with steel would not only save the solar industry money and cut back on carbon emissions, it would also provide more physical support to bigger and heavier solar panels.

Welser, an Austrian company with origins dating back to the 1660s, is a leader in roll-form steel profiles typically only seen in aluminum extrusions and helped produce a steel frame that’s easy for panel manufacturers to assemble and contractors to handle.

“What’s special about Welser Profile is we pre-notch features in the material before it gets formed,” said Bill Johnson, North America CEO of Welser Profile. “Everything about the solar industry is about how do we make it more efficient, cheaper, faster, better? You do that by all these little details to add value farther up the stream that minimizes labor, install cost. Our hole patterns and other features allow operators to snap things together, not bolt or weld things. Everyone is looking at how to make this work in a Lego setup, not a high-intense labor workforce installing all these panels.”.

Sources indicate that welser is helping bring the Origami Solar idea to life, but the fresh owner of the tech, Nextpower, is delivering steel frames to the masses. Nextpower, a steel expert through its experience in producing tracking and mounting systems, acquired Origami in 2025 and will use its existing network of steel partners to convince more PV project developers to consider an alternative to aluminum.

Recent findings suggest that “Nextpower has released over 30 manufacturing facilities in the U.S. since 2020. Nextpower buys over 700,000 short tons of primary U.S. steel annually, which is more than a small car company,” said Jenya Meydbray, VP and general manager of Nextpower’s steel frames business. “Nextpower has had [the steel frame] for one year, building on the years of Origami’s engineering with Welser’s support. What we’re doing today is launching into high-scale, high-volume production here in Ohio.”.

The solar industry defaulted to aluminum panel frames because the material is lightweight, easy to handle and less susceptible to corrosion. But as the solar industry matured, more environmental and practical issues became associated with the metal. Aluminum production on average has a five-times larger carbon footprint than steel production, a difficult point to ignore in the inherently green solar industry. Solar panels have also gotten larger in surface area and use less glass to cut weight. Aluminum might no longer be the ideal material to physically support these “major, floppy modules.”.

A steel coil feeds into a roll-forming machine producing solar panel frames. Credit: Nextpower.

Sources indicate that “Steel provides a far better structural support for the [panel] than aluminum does. That was the initial observation that the Origami founders made,” Meydbray remarked. “They landed on this specific [roll-form] profile. Roll-forming is a precision process. We’re making millions of sticks of solar panel frames a month, and all of them have to be within sub-millimeter of precision across the full length. Welser is 100 years older than America, so Welser is definitely the most experienced in this art form of steel roll-forming.”.

Recent findings suggest that welser set up North American operations in 2018 after acquiring an automotive roll-form operation in Valley City. The tech giant established a second location in the same industrial park to accommodate its growing client base in the solar, storage and energy industries.

In a recent development, welser was one of the first roll-form partners to validate Magnelis — a zinc magnesium coating that has “self-healing” properties is capable of lasting 25 years in the field — and found it a great steel coating for solar energy applications. It’s one of the features of NX CoreFrame, Nextpower’s steel solar module frame.

“Coming up with a new coating on steel, you don’t just throw it on the steel and sell it to the market. You have to trial it, validate it, make sure it works,” Johnson said. “Raw zinc — the coating has to be too thick for the longevity that the solar industry needs. Magnelis can go much lighter coating and still produce the same salt spray, same longevity, and it’s cheaper, faster, smarter.”.

Wesler is the latest high-volume production facility for NX CoreFrame, and Nextpower plans to reach 6.5 GW of annual production through additional manufacturing partners across the country.

With an established steel frame design, the product just needs to find a place on panel manufacturer’s production lines. Origami Solar had been signing supply agreements with U.S. panel assemblers, an activity that has only increased with the Nextpower transition. Meydbray said the pitch for a domestic supply chain has become more attractive, especially with Nextpower’s established regional steel manufacturing network.

Industry observers note that A machine treats steel coil as it travels along a factory line. Credit: Nextpower.

It has been revealed that “Steel strengthens the supply chain of domestic manufacturing facilities. When frames are bought overseas, they spend five, six weeks on the water before they actually arrive to the factory. [Panel companies] have about 2,000 pallets of frames in inventory when they source from overseas,” he said. “We’re able to provide actual just-in-time delivery to our factory clients. We can make deliveries every 48 hours. [They can save room] where they used to have pallets stacked up. There’s also the working capital of having stuff sit on the water for six weeks. Solar panel manufacturing is not a high-margin business, and working capital management is critical.”.

Nextpower has inked supply agreements with many multi-gigawatt panel manufacturers in the United States, including Jinko, T1 and Thornova.

Industry observers note that “This integration of Nextpower steel frames allows us to deliver high-performance modules tailored to the evolving U.S. market,” said Andrea Bodenhagen, global marketing director at Thornova Solar, which is establishing domestic solar cell manufacturing in Oklahoma. “By incorporating U.S.-made steel frames, we strengthen supply chain resilience while helping our customers maximize domestic content and improve project economics.”.

With bonus incentives from the investment tax credit still in play when solar projects use domestic products, an American-made steel frame can make all the difference.

It has been revealed that “When we see projects that have 100% domestic content on the tracker, we know that’s a perfect candidate for steel frames,” Meydbray noted. “Steel frames get 6% domestic content credit. It’s the second cheapest percent after the tracker. A domestically made solar cell is a lot more expensive than an imported solar cell. The frame is the second-most cost-effective way to buy percentage points.”.

It has been revealed that the NX CoreFrame is universal and can be used with any brand’s mounting or tracking system, but there are advantages when the project can be designed more cohesively through one supplier. Nextpower has spent the last year expanding beyond mounting systems, now offering inverter, electrical balance of system and panel products.

“[Nextpower] is ambitious, but it’s not arrogant. It prioritizes the customer relationships it’s built over the years. We spent time with our customers asking where their pain points are and expanded the business accordingly …  the organization that makes the thing the solar panel is mounted to is the same company that makes the frame that’s being mounted,” Meydbray remarked.

Industry News: Europe’s Inland Shipping Models Underprice Green Fuels. Market Prices Favor Battery Swapping.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (932 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that europe’s inland-shipping models underprice renewable diesel.
  • According to recent reports, the gap between the modeled HVO price and observed market prices matters for the investment choices these studies inform.
  • The Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine (CCNR) commissioned the original transition study behind its 2021 roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that europe’s inland-shipping models underprice renewable diesel. For a latest 110-meter dry-cargo vessel, PLATINA4Action calculates HVO (hydrotreated vegetable oil) propulsion at €1,798/day against €1,964/day for battery swapping. Apply the observed October 2026 Dutch HVO market price, including delivery, and the HVO cost is €2,515/day. Battery swapping is €551/day cheaper. The model’s claim of an HVO cost advantage fails a market-price check.

According to recent reports, the gap between the modeled HVO price and observed market prices matters for the investment choices these studies inform. It also exposes a wider pattern. European studies give renewable liquid fuels favorable future prices while expecting marine batteries to remain expensive for much longer than the broader battery market suggests.

The Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine (CCNR) commissioned the original transition study behind its 2021 roadmap. Its scenarios influenced subsequent work, including the EU-linked PLATINA4Action and SYNERGETICS projects. Those projects do not all use identical models, but their assumptions and recommendations contribute to a shared policy picture in which several combustion pathways are expected to remain competitive with direct electrification.

In the full TFIE assessment, I converted the October 2026 Dutch Class II HVO wholesale benchmark, added a delivery allowance and expressed the result in 2025 euros. The market-based HVO cost is €2.59/kg. Battery swapping becomes cheaper than HVO in the PLATINA4Action 110-meter vessel comparison at approximately €1.93/kg. At that observed market price, modeled HVO propulsion costs €2,515/day over the model’s 2028–2047 ownership period, against €1,964/day for swapping. The model puts fossil diesel at €1,844/day, leaving swapping about 7% above diesel but 22% below market-priced HVO.

Sources indicate that the price difference matters to freight operators. CCNR’s 2026 cost indices allocate fuel 35% of dry-bulk costs, 30% of tanker costs and 28% of container shipping costs. Operators compete for cargo against rivals still burning diesel. Expensive alternative fuels cannot be passed through to customers merely because a transition scenario requires them.

In a recent development, an April 2025 statement from European inland shipping and port organizations called for enough HVO at diesel-competitive prices to supply 1.6 million tons annually by around 2030. That quantity roughly matches the sector’s entire conventional diesel consumption in 2015. It exceeds the EU’s 2025 sustainable aviation fuel supply of 1.1 million tons by about 45%.

Sources indicate that HVO and conventional biodiesel compete for oils and fats also used to produce aviation fuel. Aviation has fewer practical routes to electrification, and its European mandates create demand for renewable kerosene. An HVO-centered inland strategy puts barges in direct competition with aircraft for constrained feedstocks, even where barges can draw electricity from a corridor network.

According to recent reports, synthetic fuels present an even sharper problem. SYNERGETICS gives green methanol from biological and synthetic routes a combined low wholesale price of €350/t in its stated-policy case from 2035. That same scenario uses a low green-hydrogen price of €3.50/kg. Producing a ton of synthetic methanol takes about 190 kilograms of hydrogen, costing €665 before carbon dioxide, synthesis, financing and delivery. The hydrogen input alone costs almost twice the assumed low finished-fuel price.

It has been revealed that biomethanol is a different production route. It can be made from agricultural and forestry residues, and I expect it to play a useful role in deep-sea shipping. Grouping biological and synthetic methanol together conceals the economics of each. For inland waterways, the relevant competitor is often electricity delivered directly to the propeller, not fossil methanol replaced with greener methanol.

Recent findings suggest that the battery forecasts lean in the opposite direction. SYNERGETICS places 2030 marine battery storage at €210–€520/kWh, a €365 midpoint. My inland freight electrification report models standardized marine battery containers at €100/kWh in 2030, including the marine safety and container systems, with vessel integration costed separately. A €265/kWh difference adds €1.06 million to a 4 MWh battery installation before operating the vessel. The full fleet-level analysis also prices spare batteries, financing, charging infrastructure and equipment held in reserve.

The studies’ fleet assumptions compound the fuel-price choices. One PLATINA4Action case requires a large Rhine or Danube pusher to go seven days without replenishing energy, excluding intermediate charging or exchange from the test. The SYNERGETICS SYNFEED model starts every newly introduced vessel with a Stage V combustion engine, leaving electrification to later retrofits. Those are consequential design choices for a transition modeled through 2050.

Industry observers note that freight demand should be modeled before fuel demand. Mineral oil products, coal and iron ore accounted for 35.7% of Rhine cargo mass in 2025. CCNR’s own underlying economic projections point toward large declines in coal, refining and primary metals, even as construction and trade grow. The amount and composition of freight needing propulsion in 2050 will differ from today’s cargo mix.

Recent findings suggest that the Netherlands has already reduced its 2040 hydrogen demand expectations and identified electricity as the main inland-shipping pathway toward 2050. CCNR is revisiting its transition work. The newly introduced analysis should start with the freight that will actually move, calculate route energy and charging or exchange needs, and then test the remaining fuel demand against prices reflecting aviation, deep-sea shipping and industrial competition.

Technology neutrality is a method of comparing alternatives, not an obligation to finance every fuel pathway. With HVO priced against market evidence and batteries costed realistically, the investment case for parallel fuel infrastructure weakens.

Sources indicate that the full TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment walks through the CCNR, PLATINA4Action and SYNERGETICS cost assumptions, the HVO crossover and the synthetic-fuel arithmetic. The open inland freight electrification report contains the route, fleet and infrastructure model.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes fresh gimmick functionality within major updates to its software. The recent release of V15, software for Tesla's latest in-car computers, adds another trick: A new camera angle that demonstrates the car from a third-person view, like in a video game. Tesla calls it Reality View, and out of everything a Tesla can do, it sure is one of the things.

Sources indicate that the Tesla faithful call the software update V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue. The update did include functional changes to FSD, mostly relating to the computer vision wall Tesla keeps beating its head against, but it seems the engineers had a thought while working on all those cameras: Why not use them to simulate a third-person view, like a video game?

FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines! 🤯🙌🏽 @Tesla @TeslaSI @elonmusk pic.twitter.com/m3fn7c4obA.

Initially, after looking at both Tesla's demo footage and footage from real owners, I figured the car was using SpaceXAI's models to generate a third-person view based on the input from the cameras — a method that would explain some of the odd glitches and scale challenges present in some of the clips as AI hallucinations. According to Elon Musk's tweets, that's exactly what's going on — rather than an actual display of what the car's cameras and FSD software see, Tesla owners are now treated to an AI-generated picture of what's going on around them.

The ability to mesh multiple cameras into a single point of view like this is neat, and the underlying tech is impressive, though it's unclear how much compute is needed to generate these images, and what kind of load that puts on the car. What these images aren't, though, are replacements for the actual data visualization that FSD used to supply. Even Tesla owners are admitting confusion between objects the car does and doesn't see with the upcoming display. Most Tesla party tricks are some ratio of neat to useless, but this one genuinely appears to make the user experience of FSD worse.

Industry observers note that unlike other small EVs, the IONIQ 3 makes a strong case for itself as your only car, not a tender to the massive family SUV. For the money nothing can compete with the range, the space and the efficiency. —Ollie Kew, Deputy Editor of Top Gear.

It is a great recognition of the work that has gone into developing IONIQ 3. —Christopher McKinnon, Vice President, Head of Product and Product Director Office for Europe at Hyundai Motor Europe.

IONIQ 3 was designed and developed specifically for European customers and is produced at Hyundai Motor Türkiye’s İzmit plant.

Industry observers note that top Gear’s editorial team highlighted the combination of value for money, distinctive design, interior space and driving efficiency. Despite its compact exterior dimensions, IONIQ 3 offers the range and practicality to serve as a customer’s primary vehicle.

The recognition continues Hyundai Motor’s success at the TopGear.com Awards. INSTER was named Supermini of the Year at the 2026 awards, while IONIQ 9 received the Best Seven-Seat EV title at the 2025 TopGear.com Electric Awards.

Selected by the editorial team behind BBC Top Gear magazine and TopGear.com, the awards celebrate automotive excellence in areas including performance, innovation and driving appeal. Industry observers note that the 1970s band Nazareth warned us that Love Hurts. Today's Nice Price or No Dice Alfa Romeo has looks that could make you fall in love, but also a brand reputation for tempestuousness that might cause pain — financial and otherwise. Let's find out if this one is priced to make that pain hurt so good.

Legend has it that, though the execs at Land Rover tasked company stylist David Bache with designing the bodywork of the in-development Range Rover, they were so taken with the styling of the engineering mules that, with minor tweaks, that became the truck's first and final design.

The 1987 Range Rover Classic we looked at on Tuesday differed from that original design with a modified grille and, more importantly, four doors, as the earlier two-door model was never offered for sale in the U.S. Our Range Rover was claimed to have been restored, and while there remained some boogers under its desk, it did look to be in serviceable overall shape. That wasn't enough to get the vast majority of you on board with the idea of spending the $28,850 the seller asked for its sale. Ultimately, that price fell in a 93% 'No Dice' loss.

I'd like to get one thing out of the way up front: I find today's 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia incredibly good-looking, with no bad angles from which to view it. I mention that because my prose describing the car might be a bit biased by the siren's song of the car's Helen-of-Troy-build-a-substantial-horse-beat-up-the-Trojans level of good looks.

Of course, like Helen's legendary beauty and the battles fought by suitors for the opportunity to awkwardly sit at her knee and stare stupidly into her limpid pool eyes, owning an Alfa Romeo of any ilk could lead to devastation.

In a recent development, alfa had to get the Giulia's looks just right, a necessity that went so far as to delay the car's launch. Fiat boss Sergio Marchionne kept rejecting designs Alfa's internal Centro Stile Alfa Romeo designers offered during the car's development, claiming they weren't good-looking enough. Why Alfa didn't go the route of having a design house like Pininfarina pen the car is a mystery, although traditionally Alfa handled saloon styling in-house while farming out coupes to such esteemed external designers, so there's that.

According to recent reports, regardless, Alfa got the Giulia's looks right, and didn't screw up the car's underpinnings either. Rolling on a then-newly introduced RWD platform developed with oversight by Ferrari engineer Philippe Krief, the Giulia has the goods to compete with the likes of BMW's 3 Series and Audi A4 when the roads get bendy. It's a testament to how good the basic chassis is that it can perform competently with this base four-cylinder model and, with notable tweaks, also with the monster 500-horsepower V6 Quadrifoglio.

In a recent development, our car has the 1,995cc DOHC MultiAir four under the hood. With variable valve timing and an intercooled turbocharger, that makes an astounding 280 hp and 306 pound-feet of torque. Matched to that engine is a ZF 8HP50 8-speed automatic transmission that powers the rear wheels. While AWD was offered on this model, this car's RWD layout is simpler to maintain and lighter, offering better performance and fuel economy.

In a recent development, according to the ad, this Giulia has 75,000 miles on the clock and, remarkable for any Alfa, especially a first-year model that may still be suffering teething pains, it is claimed to suffer no complications whatsoever. Did I mention it's also really good-looking?

Industry observers note that having established that this is a very attractive car, it's also in very good shape. The pictures in the ad support the seller's claim that it's "well kept," as the Silverstone Gray Metallic paint appears to have no dents, and the darker gray factory alloys show no evidence of curb rash.

This being an entry-level model and with the ad's limited description, the seating surfaces are likely vinyl rather than leather. Some wood on the console warms up the space in an otherwise Germanic, all-black (even the Alfa badge) interior.

That's not to say that the car is parsimoniously equipped, as it has all the basic comfort and convenience features one might expect on a reasonably modern car. Those include power windows, locks, seats and mirrors, dual-zone climate control with eyeball vents for the back seats, and a center stack screen for infotainment and the backup camera display. There's also cruise control, auto headlamps... You name it, it's likely got it.

Per the seller, the car presents in excellent condition, has a clean title, and drives perfectly. What more could one want?

In a recent development, well, I'm sure one thing we could all ask for is a car that's free and can navigate to a leprechaun's pot of gold when asked. There are certain things we can't have, no matter how much we want them.

This car isn't free, but its $7,999 asking price is a recent reduction from $8,500, and it makes one wonder: just how scared are people about buying a decade-old, out-of-warranty Alfa that even that slightly higher price seemingly couldn't get a nibble?

Naturally, you'll suss it out in the comments and, ultimately, judge it in the vote. With that in mind, what's your take on this base-but-far-from-basic Giulia and that new, lower $7,999 asking price? Is that a handsome deal on this beauty of a car? Or, even at that modest amount, could buying this Alfa get ugly real fast?

Joint Letter on the Revision of the CO₂ Emission Standards for Cars & Vans

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Dear Climate and Environment Ministers of the European Union,.
  • We, a broad coalition representing non-governmental organizations, think tanks, energy providers, renewable and cleantech industries, and the e-mobility sector, are writing to express our concern over the current direction of EU discussions on the revision of the cars and vans CO₂ emission standards regulation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Counting combustion vehicles as clean would blur the market signal and bring back the very uncertainty that carmakers, suppliers, and investors cannot afford. Manufacturers could meet their targets without selling a single electric car.

Dear Climate and Environment Ministers of the European Union,.

We, a broad coalition representing non-governmental organizations, think tanks, energy providers, renewable and cleantech industries, and the e-mobility sector, are writing to express our concern over the current direction of EU discussions on the revision of the cars and vans CO₂ emission standards regulation.

Sources indicate that road transport remains the primary driver of Europe’s oil dependency. This structural vulnerability costs the EU hundreds of billions of euros annually, weakens our economy, and leaves citizens exposed to geopolitical shocks. The second fossil fuel crisis in just four years has already added more than €50 billion to Europe’s energy bill, hitting households and businesses hard.

Our continued reliance on fossil fuels also accelerates the climate crisis. This summer, Europeans paid the price as successive heatwaves brought record temperatures, devastating wildfires, and severe droughts across the continent. Transport remains the EU’s biggest emitter, with cars and vans alone accounting for 16% of total CO₂ emissions.

Yet while the market is moving rapidly, political discussions are falling out of touch with reality.

According to recent reports, europe already has a mature, increasingly affordable and readily available structural solution in electric vehicles – which are also the most effective way to shield consumers from volatile fuel prices. Electric vehicles are scaling fast, reaching a record 27% market share in the third quarter of 2026 in the EU.

Instead of building on this momentum, discussions in the Council on the car CO₂ regulation threaten to slow the EV trajectory and inject uncertainty for companies and consumers. Most concerning is the proposal to create a latest category for combustion cars running on e-fuels and biofuels, so-called “vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels” (VEEFs), and count them as zero-emission vehicles.

Too much attention is being paid to combustion-based technologies, distracting from the electric future. Cars running on these fuels still burn fuel in a combustion engine; treating them on par with battery electric vehicles would create a false and unfair equivalence. Under this proposal, manufacturers could meet their targets without selling a single electric car.

According to recent reports, counting combustion vehicles as clean would blur the market signal and bring back the very uncertainty that carmakers, suppliers, and investors cannot afford. It would penalize businesses that are scaling up today and jeopardize the €200 billion already invested in the battery-electric transition. Europe cannot compete globally on electric cars if targets are weakened and undue credit is given to e-fuels, biofuels and hybrids.

We must reset this narrative on vehicle electrification. Europe’s clean industry needs investment certainty and regulatory stability. We therefore call on Climate and Environment Ministers to safeguard the car and van CO₂ targets adopted just three years ago, reject any weakening of the 2030 and 2035 ambition, and remove the “vehicles running exclusively on eligible fuels” (VEEFs) category.

Now is the time for political leadership. Member States have the chance to ensure this fossil fuel crisis is Europe’s last, and to act decisively to build a clean, sovereign, and affordable mobility system supported by a strong EU clean industry.

Download the letter to see the full list of signatories.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From an objective standpoint, cars are difficult things to justify. They are prohibitively expensive to buy, fuel, insure, maintain, and repair. They pollute, they kill pedestrians (and people in other cars), and they are a categorically flawed form of mass transportation. They are also really interesting, exciting, fun, private, and convenient, and in many parts of the real world, they're often a necessary component of daily life. It can feel like a complex duality to hold the love of cars in tandem with an understanding of their downsides, but doing so has made me appreciate every car on the road. Having said that, every now and then I'll see a car on the road and think, "thank goodness that's not being made anymore.".

In a recent development, you've likely said the same thing to yourself, which brings me to today's question: I want to know which car you're glad is dead. Whether it's a personal vendetta against a certain model that ran over your RC car as a kid, or a model that drained your wallet and tested your patience when you owned it, share your answer in the comments section below.

Recent findings suggest that I'm taking the most obvious route here and saying that I'm glad the Tesla Cybertruck is dead. Though it's technically not slated to end production until next year, I'm counting it because it is such a hateful vehicle, it deserves the accolade. Sometimes I wonder if the Cybertruck would've been received as cool in an alternate reality where Tesla's CEO isn't a cringey spoiled megalomaniac loser, but I guess the world will never know.

In a recent development, in the context of our present reality, everything about the Cybertruck came off as a tarnished middle finger to the idea of sensibility, rationality, and logic, as well as a middle finger to every other road user, thanks to the sharp edges of its stainless steel body panels. If you think I'm being dramatic, know that its edges are so sharp, in fact, that the United Kingdom refused to glitch the Cybertruck a certificate of conformity to the UK's vehicle safety standards. UK police publicly seized a Cybertruck that someone was illegally using on British roads, saying, "whilst this may seem trivial to some, legitimate concerns exist around the safety of other road users or pedestrians if they were involved in a collision with a Cybertruck.".

I feel like the world will be a better place once the Cybertruck is out of production, so I'm glad it's dead. What car are you glad is dead?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that good morning! It's Wednesday, November 25, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most crucial stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

Sources indicate that in this morning's edition, the U.S. and Canada are still at odds on auto tariffs as the trade war continues, an ex-Volkswagen engineer pleads guilty to inside trading over the tech giant's deal with Rivian, Stellantis is suing the Unifor union for alleged "obstruction" of environmental work at Brampton plant and Amazon Autos is heading to the UK.

With everything else going on in the world at the moment, you'd be forgiven for forgetting that there's an entire trade war happening between the U.S. and Canada right now, but I'm here to remind you that bad boy is still raging. Much of that is thanks to auto tariffs — one of the major sticking points dividing the two North American countries as negotiations heat back up following a last-minute collapse this summer.

According to recent reports, automotive and other key industrial sectors, like steel, are holding up a deal that could end the two-year trade war. President Trump enacted a 25% tariff on auto imports in April of 2025, and Canada came right back with its own in-kind duties soon after. It's a real mess, and it's driving up costs for everyone. Obviously, this didn't need to happen. Trump didn't need to do this, but here we are. From Automotive News:.

It has been revealed that both sets of tariffs include exemptions for locally made parts, which lowers the effective tariff rate on Canadian vehicles exported to the United States to about 12.5 per cent and U.S. exports to Canada to about 21.25 per cent — though the exact rate varies by plant and model.

Trump has repeatedly claimed the United States does not need Canadian-made cars and pressed automakers to shift production south of the border. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has maintained that any agreement with the United States must leave Canada with a viable auto sector.

Ottawa has been pushing for a deal that will put the effective tariff rate for Canadian vehicle exports to the United States on an even keel with those built south of the border but has been hard-pressed to get there, [Automotive Parts Manufacturers' Association president, Flavio] Volpe mentioned.

As negotiators closed in on a deal this summer by pitching a broader parts exemption, the U.S. offer would have left Canadian autos facing up an effective tariff of up to 7.5 per cent tariffs, he stated. While an improvement over the roughly 12.5 per cent rate automakers face today, it is still higher than the industry's profit margin, making it too high for Ottawa to accept, Volpe added.

Canadian negotiators are "not religious" about what mechanism is used to bring the effective tariff rate down, Volpe mentioned, but want to put plants on both sides of the border back on an even playing field.

Counterintuitively, U.S. assembly plants are not immune to tariffs.

Parts compliant with the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement reach U.S. assembly lines tariff-free, but American-made vehicles compliant with the trade deal can include 25 per cent parts content from overseas. That content faces up to 25-per-cent tariffs, translating into a tariff rate on U.S.-made vehicles of as much as 6.5 per cent.

Recent findings suggest that A 3.75-per-cent MSRP credit for American-made vehicles offered by the U.S. Department of Commerce — effective through 2030 — offsets part of these added costs.

But even automakers building USMCA-compliant vehicles in the United States can face an effective tariff rate of 2.75 per cent. The tally can be more or less, depending on where companies source their parts.

In a recent development, the five automakers that at the moment produce vehicles in Canada — the Substantial Three, Honda and Toyota — are pushing hard for an interim deal that would close or eliminate the tariff gap between Canadian and U.S. plants, even if it's a short-term solution.

Right now, there's no real timetable for when a deal could be reached, though Canadian pundits are actually aware that Trump has threatened to hike tariffs to 50% at the start of 2027. While they don't think it'll happen, with Trump, it can never be truly ruled out.

A former Volkswagen engineer pleaded guilty to insider trading based on secret information he possessed about the automaker's planned $5 billion joint venture with electric vehicle maker Rivian. Michael Stamp pleaded guilty to securities fraud in a Manhattan federal court as part of a deal with prosecutors, confessing that he used his brokerage accounts to buy Rivian shares and options while in possession of confidential information about the merger that he had learned from another employee.

Recent findings suggest that as we previously reported, the 31-year-old and another former VW engineer, Marcus Plank, were charged in July with making a combined $300,000 trading before the Rivian deal was confirmed publicly. Prosecutors stated Stamp made a cool quarter million, and Plank made $50,000 while also passing information to a family member who made $12,000. From Bloomberg:.

"I knew that what I was doing was wrong and a breach of my duty to my employer," Stamp said at a hearing before a federal judge.

Volkswagen and Rivian announced the deal on June 26, 2024, giving Rivian a financial lifeline as manufacturers large and small began to rethink strategies in a slowing market for electric vehicles.

Stamp and Plank, who were both living in San Jose, California, while on assignment from Germany, were initially charged with conspiracy and securities fraud and faced as much as 25 years in prison if convicted of the most serious counts at trial. Plank has pleaded not guilty and is free on a $500,000 bond.

According to recent reports, prosecutors said internet searches made around the time of the crimes indicated that the two men knew what they were doing was illegal. Just eight days before the announcement, Stamp — that goofus — searched for "statute of limitations insider trading," according to the government. Soon after, Plank's aforementioned family member searched in German "how is insider trading prosecuted?".

Well, substantial dog, this is how it's prosecuted — unless you're very rich or in Congress.

There's another fun chapter in the war over Stellantis' Brampton Assembly plant in Ontario, Canada. Now, it's spilled over into court as the automaker has filed a lawsuit against the Unifor workers' union, alleging it is impeding an environmental assessment necessary for the sale to defense contractor Roshel to go through.

According to recent reports, in documents filed in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, Stellantis said it is seeking an injunction that would require the union, its national president Lana Payne and Unifor Local 1285 plant chairperson Ardis Snow to stop blocking the Brampton plant and preventing work at the site. The tech giant wants the court to declare that the union has trespassed at the facility and "obstructed the lawful entrance to and exit from the premises." From Automotive News:.

A statement of claim remarked union officials are "physically preventing, impeding, and restricting Stellantis' ability to provide access to the premises" to environmental consulting firm Pinchin Ltd.

Pinchin was retained by Roshel — the armoured vehicle manufacturer that agreed to buy the idled Brampton plant from Stellantis for an undisclosed amount earlier this month — to carry out environmental work starting Nov. 9, according to the documents.

However, Stellantis mentioned that morning, union representatives blockaded entrances to the plant with trucks, pylons and individuals carrying Unifor flags and that Unifor told the automaker it wouldn't let Pinchin personnel or equipment through.

"To date, Unifor has continued to obstruct access by persons associated with the environmental work, and Pinchin has not been permitted to perform the environmental work," the statement of claim noted.

"Despite Stellantis' reasonable efforts to obtain police assistance, those efforts have not brought the obstruction of or interference with lawful access to the premises under an acceptable degree of control, nor has Pinchin been permitted to access the premises.".

The allegations have not been tested in court.

The statement of claim remarked Stellantis "is suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable harm and other losses," although the extent of those losses "are extremely difficult, if not impossible, to quantify in monetary terms.".

It added that "continued obstruction" of the environmental assessment "threatens to delay or prevent completion of a material diligence step, interfere with the timetable for the proposed transaction, and affect the responsibilities of Stellantis and Roshel following closing of the proposed transaction.".

Stellantis' deal with Roshel is expected to close in mid-December, subject to certain conditions, according to the documents.

In response, Unifor said it has been "demonstrating in support of Canadian jobs at the Brampton plant throughout the past year." Payne said that the sale of the plant to Roshel is "unacceptable" to the union, and it will continue to work with all parties to get a different outcome.

Astelia’s autonomous network mitigation blocks AI-driven exploits without a patch

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Exposure management company Astelia Inc.
  • The upcoming capability has been designed to address what Astelia claims is the problem of frontier AI models cutting the time to exploit to almost zero, leaving manual triage and remediation unable to keep up.
  • “For years, security teams have been told to patch faster,” remarked co-founder and Chief Executive Alon Noy, adding that the advice “stops working when the exploit arrives before the change window does.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Exposure management company Astelia Inc. today unveiled the launch of autonomous network mitigation, a new capability that allows organizations to block artificial intelligence-driven exploits at the network level, even when a patch isn’t available or can’t be applied.

The upcoming capability has been designed to address what Astelia claims is the problem of frontier AI models cutting the time to exploit to almost zero, leaving manual triage and remediation unable to keep up. Astelia argues that autonomous remediation isn’t a viable option for large enterprises, where every patch requires a change window so it doesn’t break important business processes. In many cases, there is also no patch to apply because the vendor hasn’t released a fix yet or, for older and end-of-life systems, never will.

“For years, security teams have been told to patch faster,” remarked co-founder and Chief Executive Alon Noy, adding that the advice “stops working when the exploit arrives before the change window does.”.

In a recent development, autonomous network mitigation is designed to block the path an attacker would use to reach a vulnerable system instead of changing the system itself. Mitigations are applied automatically within policies the organization sets. Nothing on the asset is changed, allowing business-critical systems, including operational technology, to stay online.

Industry observers note that underpinning the service is Astelia’s reachability analysis, which maps an organization’s real network topology and applies agentic AI to analyze the requirements of each exploit. By correlating exploit conditions with network topology, the platform identifies which vulnerabilities are reachable by attackers and through which paths. In one enterprise deployment, approximately 40 million vulnerabilities were reduced to fewer than 2,000 that were reachable, according to the organization.

It has been revealed that key features of autonomous network mitigation include the ability to identify the most effective choke point on an attack path and drive the mitigation through an organization’s web application firewall or intrusion prevention and detection system. A single rule at a choke point is said to protect every vulnerable server behind it, compared with one change per server when patching. Because mitigations are only applied to paths that have been proven reachable, the service doesn’t add rules for exposure that doesn’t exist.

Sources indicate that every mitigation applied by Astelia can also be rolled back, something that isn’t always possible with a patch. That is remarked to allow teams to act swiftly without putting business operations at risk.

Autonomous network mitigation can be deployed through Astelia Agents, the manufacturer’s suite of AI agents, as a dedicated agent that applies mitigations on its own. The agent can also be connected with other agents to respond to urgent threats such as zero-day vulnerabilities and critical disclosures. Astelia gave the example of the PHP2Shell remote code execution flaws disclosed in October, which left end-of-life PHP servers with no official fix.

Recent findings suggest that each organization sets its own guardrails on how mitigations are applied. People can require human approval for specific environments or actions, according to the company. Every action is logged and can be audited. Analysis on the Astelia platform continues to run on read-only integrations, with mitigation actions using scoped permissions that each organization enables and controls.

Autonomous network mitigation initially supports web application firewall and intrusion prevention and detection rules, with support for firewall rules planned in the future.

In a recent development, founded in 2024 by former leaders of the Israeli National Red Team, Astelia is a venture capital-backed company that raised $35 million in combined seed and Series A funding in February. Investors in the company include Index Ventures, Team8 and Holly Ventures.
